articles.title: Deadly Grand Canyon flooding knocks out critical water line amid race to find missing hikers
articles.summary: A 46-year-old man was found dead in the Colorado River as search, and rescue teams race to locate 15 missing hikers in the Grand Canyon area.
articles.body: Severe flash flooding knocked out a central water line in the Grand Canyon this weekend, forcing the National Park Service to implement strict water restrictions amid an ongoing race to find missing hikers. NPS says it will implement stage four water restrictions beginning at 12:00 p.m. on Monday, saying the Saturday flooding caused "extensive damage to infrastructure," including the Transcanyon Waterline that supplies the park with water. Park officials say one person was killed and 15 may be missing after the flooding, though they say that is an estimate. Park officials confirmed they recovered the body of a 46-year-old man from the Colorado River on Sunday night. He has not been publicly identified. MISSING GRAND CANYON HIKER, 83, RESCUED AFTER GETTING SEPARATED FROM COMPANION NPS issued a request for the public to provide information on the 15 other people who are believed to be missing. "The National Park Service is asking anyone who knows of hikers or backpackers who were in the inner canyon along the Bright Angel Creek corridor on August 29, as well as anyone who had a campground reservation in the affected corridor, to provide information to the National Park Service Investigative Services Branch," NPS said in a statement. AMERICAN HIKER VANISHES ON TROPICAL TREK AS FLASH FLOODS, MUDSLIDES TURN JUNGLE GETAWAY INTO DESPERATE SEARCH Park officials say they have so far evacuated at least 62 people since the Saturday flooding. The stage 4 water restrictions affecting the rest of the park include forced dry camping with no access to water spigots, the temporary closure of overnight lodgings, and a strict no-fire rule for the South Rim and inner canyon areas. ARMY BLACK HAWKS AIRLIFT 200-PLUS STRANDED CAMPERS AS MISSOURI FLOODS TRIGGER MORE 350 RESCUES The flooding struck Bright Angel Canyon and the Phantom Ranch area on Aug. 29, according to NPS, which added that nearly all footbridges spanning Bright Angel Creek were destroyed. Arizona Gov. Katie Hobbs said state emergency officials are coordinating with federal and local authorities as the search continues. EXPERTS ZERO IN ON LIKELY CAUSE OF DEADLY NEPAL MUDSLIDE, WITH MORE THAN 1,400 MISSING "My heart is with the families and loved ones of every person unaccounted for after the flash flooding at the Grand Canyon," Hobbs wrote on X. "DEMA is coordinating with NPS and Coconino County Emergency Management to support search and recovery efforts." Arizona Secretary of State Adrian Fontes called the flash flooding "devastating" and thanked first responders for searching for those still unaccounted for and evacuating others from the affected area. articles.title: Search continues for 18 passengers after ferry capsized in northern Cyprus
articles.summary: Eight people have died after the ferry started taking on water shortly after setting off for Turkey.
articles.body:
Rescuers are continuing their search for 18 passengers of a ferry which capsized off the coast of northern Cyprus on Sunday.

The vessel, which was carrying 259 passengers and eight crew members, began taking on water soon after departing the coastal town of Kyrenia in the self-proclaimed Turkish republic on Cyprus.

Eight people have been confirmed to have died in the incident, while 19 are currently being treated at hospitals in northern Cyprus, local authorities say.

The ship's captain, seven crew members, and another man were arrested on Monday, while warrants have been issued for a further seven people.

Ünal Üstel, Prime Minister of the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus (TRNC), which is only recognised by Turkey, announced a three-day period of national mourning.

The boat has completely sunk and is lying at a depth of 514m (1,686ft), officials say.

Debris remains scattered across the water, including a black wheelie suitcase bobbing on the surface and a sheet of steel that appeared to have broken away from the ferry.

Authorities are attempting to recover the vessel's black box recorder to establish what happened.

The privately owned ferry left the popular holiday resort of Kyrenia at about 12:30 (09:30 GMT), en route to the town of Tasucu in Turkey.

It had been scheduled to travel to Turkey on Saturday but its journey was delayed due to poor weather conditions.

Üstel told local media the boat was hit by two waves before it capsized.

While the captain of the vessel was trying to recover from the first wave, a second wave hit and it began taking on water, he said.

Among the missing are Ayten Bicer's two children - her 12-year-old daughter Miray and six-year-old son Mehmet Asaf.

She told local media she felt Miray slip out of her hands and disappear as they tried to cling on to the overturned boat.

"She was saying, 'Don't let go'. And I didn't let go of my daughter. I swear, I didn't let her go," Bicer said.

She said a suitcase fell on top of her which forced her daughter from her grip. She managed to grab hold of her daughter's foot, but her shoes were coated in engine oil from the overturned vessel and she slipped through her hands.

She and her husband, Hayri, are by the port in Kyrenia with other families as they await news of their loved ones.

The ferry - a high-speed 40m long, 10m wide Filo Jet vessel - sails under the flag of Turkey, according to Marine Traffic.

Filo Denizcilik, the company which operates the capsized passenger boat, said it was "deeply saddened by the tragic accident".

The TRNC controls the northern third of the island of Cyprus, which has been divided since 1974.

articles.title: Rescuers search for 18 missing after boat capsizes off Northern Cyprus
articles.summary: The captain and crew of the ferry have been brought before a judge and placed under formal arrest.
articles.body:
The search is continuing for 18 missing people the day after eight people died when a ferry capsized off the coast of Northern Cyprus.

Early on Monday, the captain and eight others were brought before a judge and placed under formal arrest as three days of national mourning began, according to the official state news agency of the self-declared Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus (TRNC).

The ferry ran into trouble ⁠⁠about midday (09:00 GMT) on Sunday, shortly after leaving the northern port of Girne – also known as Kyrenia – heading for the Turkish port of Tasucu in Mersin province. It was one of several daily sea shuttle links with Turkiye.

A major rescue operation began for the 267 passengers and crew on board, according to local authorities. They said 241 were rescued, eight died and 18 were listed as missing. Their nationalities have not been published.

It was not clear if people remained trapped on the vessel, which is lying on the seabed at a depth of more than 500 metres (1,640 ft).

Passengers said the boat had begun taking on water before it capsized. Some survivors said they heard an explosion at the front of the boat, others said there was not enough safety equipment. Video from the scene broadcast by Turkish television showed the capsized ferry with passengers wearing life jackets sitting on top of its orange hull.

“Some people had to jump without lifebuoys or life jackets,” one young man, Efe Multici, told CNN Turk. “It was literally a fight for survival.”

Serkan Kunduraci, who escaped the sinking ferry by hauling himself through a broken window, said he saw children and others drowning in the sea 7.5km (4 nautical miles) off the Cypriot coast.

“I saw some who didn’t know how to swim die in the sea,” he told the DHA news agency.

“We saw and witnessed a family’s children, boys and girls, very young children, drowning.”

Rescuer Muhammed Ozcelik, who runs a water sports company, said his boat was one of the first on the scene and began hauling survivors from the sea.

“We tried to do more than we could. People were saying, ‘Take me too, take me too,’ but the capacity was full,” the Associated Press agency reported.

Recovering the vessel’s “black box” data recorder would help understand what caused the incident, authorities said.

Divers from Turkiye were assisting the ⁠⁠search, officials said.

Cyprus was split in 1974 and Turkish Cypriots declared independence from Greek control in 1983. Only Turkiye recognises the north, where more than 35,000 troops are stationed.

articles.title: An Oregon farmer grew tomatoes, potatoes, squash, garlic and beans for 40 years without irrigation; careful soil preparation kept stored moisture in the root zone
articles.summary: US News: Someone has rightly said that 'Necessity is the mother of invention'. Over decades, weather patterns became less predictable across the Pacific Northw.
articles.body: Someone has rightly said that 'Necessity is the mother of invention'. Over decades, weather patterns became less predictable across the Pacific Northwest, and farmers contended with hotter temperatures, drought and shrinking snowmelt that strained water supplies. It was then that a different method, developed over four decades of experimentation by one Oregon farmer came to the rescue. Known as Dry Farming, it is a technique for growing crops without irrigation by carefully managing the moisture already in the soil. A study published by Oregon State University in 2014 states that for 40 years (1974-2014) a farmer grew organic tomatoes, potatoes, winter squash, garlic, favas and other beans without irrigation. He started dry farming in California but moved to a 9.6-acre site near Veneta, Oregon, in 2007. The property had no water rights, but he grew food for his family and sold crops to small grocery stores in Eugene.The key is soil prepAccording to the published report, the farmer’s experience undermines the notion that dry farming is merely turning off the water. The success of dry farming depends mainly on soil preparation, moisture conservation, planting timing, soil structure, and crop spacing. And the farmer worked the soil during the first good dry spell of spring, when it was moist enough to hold together when squeezed but dry enough to crumble. Timing is everything, and it doesn’t always follow a calendar, states the report. It is reported that he first cultivated the soil, then left it for two or three weeks and cultivated again. More preparation created a good seed bed that could hold moisture in the root zone. His soil was mostly Veneta loam, but deeper layers of clay helped retain water. He also used sheep, geese and legume cover crops to build soil fertility and improve soil structure.Holding precious moisture below the soilAccording to the report, water management was important once planting began. For direct-seeded crops, the farmer planted seeds in the soil and stepped on them to ensure good contact with the soil. The soil was kept loose for about 4 to 6 inches around the plant to help the roots develop and keep the moisture in below the surface. Heavy rain or watering from above could defeat this system by compacting the soil surface. When the surface dried later it could crack and accelerate moisture loss from the layers below. Wider plant spacing also meant less competition for limited water and nutrients. The farmer also selected spacings that worked with his tractor. This made the system easier to manage, and largely a one-person operation.Selecting drought-tolerant cropsAnother important component back then was crop selection. Tomatoes, potatoes, winter squash, garlic and beans were doing well in his conditions. The farmer also saved seed from many crops. This allowed plants to become increasingly adapted to his land, over successive seasons. His tomatoes included a Big Beef that started out as a volunteer, and his Blue Hokkaido squash was the result of decades of development.Could dry farming be more important?Dryland farming might not succeed everywhere, states the report. The method may not be suitable for sandy or shallow soils with little water-holding capacity and some crops may not be suitable for it. But for growers facing water shortages, uncertain water rights or the high cost of installing irrigation, the technique could provide another tool to manage risk. The experience of the Oregon farmer proves that irrigation is not always necessary for productive agriculture. With proper soil preparation, the right crops and disciplined moisture management, stored water can potentially last plants throughout an entire growing season.Images Courtesy: istock and Oregon State UniversityCatch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: How to Clean a Washing Machine | NBC Selected
articles.summary: I learned the best way to clean a washing machine to help it work more efficiently. Here’s how cleaning experts recommend doing it.
articles.body: Even on your most thorough cleaning day, one of the last places you might prioritize is your washing machine. For an appliance that’s constantly filled with detergent and water, you probably don’t think of it as being dirty. Ironically, though, your washing machine, just like your dishwasher, air fryer and coffee maker, could use a cleaning every once in a while. Plus, cleaning a washing machine regularly helps it work better, according to Ryan Knoll, owner of home cleaning company TidyCasa. In fact, “if you’ve ever run a cycle and your clothes still smell bad, [your washer] probably needs to be cleaned,” he says. To learn more about how to clean a washing machine the right way, whether it’s a top loader or front loader, I spoke with Knoll and another cleaning expert for their guidance and the best products to help you do it. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. The best products for cleaning a washing machine We’re going to break down the simple steps for cleaning a washing machine below. But first, we’re sharing the products that you’ll need to do the job. All of the products below are either direct recommendations from our experts and/or have at least a four-star average rating from 500 or more shoppers on Amazon. These dissolving tablets from Affresh, which Knoll recommends, are easy to use to clean your washing machine. You simply add one tablet to the drum, whether it’s a top- or front-loading machine, and run it on a normal cycle with hot water. It helps remove mildew, grime and soap scum, which often forms if you have hard water. The brand recommends only using one tablet a month, so a pack of 12 will last you the whole year. Shoppers say the tablets do a great job of keeping the machine smelling clean and they love the scent it leaves behind. This washing machine cleaning powder comes in pre-portioned pouches. You can use one packet each month to clean your washer and get rid of odors. People who bought the cleaner say it does a thorough job of removing odors from their machine and that there isn’t any residual product after doing a cycle. According to Tide, it’s compatible with all types of washing machines. This set comes with 24 washing machine cleaner tablets, which the brand recommends using twice a month. The tablets help remove bad smells and residue from things like hair, according to reviewers. They also help get rid of limescale from hard water and shoppers say they remove odors from the appliance. Apple cider vinegar can do a lot of different things particularly when it comes to cleaning, including cleaning your washing machine and getting rid of odors. Knoll recommends using a cup of it to clean your machine, and then running one extra cycle to get rid of any residual vinegar. Unlike other store-bought cleaning products, it isn’t harsh and the hands and the smell doesn’t last for days. This set of brushes includes one long-handled brush and one short-handled brush, both of which are angled at the end. Both brushes are great for cleaning the gasket of your washer, and the long-handled brush is also ideal for scrubbing small crevices around the agitator and detergent compartments of your machine. How to clean a washing machine in 4 steps Below are the best steps to take to clean your washing machine, according to Knoll and Becky Rapinchuck, the owner of cleaning brand Clean Mama.* *Any product recommendations in this story were made independently of Rapinchuck, who we only consulted for guidance. We did not ask her for product recommendations. Make sure your washing machine is completely empty. Remove any small debris that might be at the bottom of the washer drum (if it’s a top-loading machine) and be sure there aren’t any small pieces of debris hidden on the inside of the drum (if it’s a front loading washer). If possible, remove the detergent and fabric softener compartments and the agitator (the thing in the middle that the clothes spin around on a top-loading washer) from the machine. Scrub them with water and mild dish soap, such as Dawn Platinum Powerwash Dish Spray, and let them dry. Alternatively, if the compartments aren’t removable, use a scrub brush or damp microfiber cloth with soap to wipe the compartments clean. If needed, use a small scrub brush to scrub away any residue. Put the compartments back into the machine.For a front-loading washing machine: Open the door and remove the rubber gasket lining it. “Front loaders are especially prone to mildew and odor because water and moisture get trapped in the rubber gasket around the door,” says Rapinchuck. Use a damp microfiber cloth to wipe the gasket clean, making sure to get in crevices. If needed, use a small brush or toothbrush to scrub away any debris or slimy residue. Put the gasket back into the door. For a top-loading washing machine: Unlike front-loading washers, top-loading machines don’t have rubber gaskets lining the door. Use a damp microfiber cloth to wipe away any debris, such as dust and hair, from the lid.Add a washing machine cleaning tablet, such as the Affresh Washing Machine Cleaner or Active Washing Machine Cleaner, a packet of powder washing machine detergent like the Tide Washing Machine Cleaner or one cup of apple cider vinegar to the drum of the washing machine. Run a regular cycle but use the hottest water setting available. Then, run one more cycle with hot water. Lastly, prop the lid or door open and let the machine air dry. Use a microfiber cloth with soap and water to wipe the exterior of the machine. How often should you clean a washing machine? You should clean your washing machine every one to four months, according to Knoll. If you have a front-loading machine you may want to clean it at least once a month since they tend to build up more residue, but it also depends on how often you do laundry and how large your loads are when you do. Meet our cleaning experts At NBC Selected, we work with experts who have specialized knowledge and authority based on relevant training and/or experience. We also take steps to ensure all expert advice and recommendations are made independently and without undisclosed financial conflicts of interest. Ryan Knoll is the owner of home cleaning company TidyCasaBecky Rapinchuck is the founder of cleaning brand and site Clean Mama.* *Any product recommendations in this story were made independently of Rapinchuck, who we only consulted for guidance. We did not ask her for product recommendations. Why trust NBC Selected? I’m a commerce editor at NBC Selected, where I write about home, kitchen and cleaning appliances. articles.title: WWE star rips 'f—ing weird' autograph-seeker after bizarre interaction while trying to catch connecting flight
articles.summary: WWE star Paige revealed a autograph-seeker bought a plane ticket just to ambush her at a connecting gate, calling the airport encounter "weirdo behavior."
articles.body: Pro wrestlers have been clear with their rabid fans – be polite, respectful and refrain from being weird when seeing them in public. WWE star Paige had to make that clear once again. articles.title: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Turkiye meet: What’s next for their defence pact?
articles.summary: As US-Iran strikes resume, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye test their pact’s substance, and who might join next.
articles.body:
Islamabad, Pakistan — Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye have formally called their new mutual-defence pact the Mecca Defence Alliance, announcing the name on Monday in Istanbul after a meeting between senior officials from the three countries.

“There is a secretariat that has been established in Riyadh, and the first secretary general will be appointed amongst our Pakistani brothers,” Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said at a press conference after the talks.

Fidan said the alliance was based on “international principles such as respecting the sovereignty of other states, territorial integrity and not intervening in internal affairs,” and that it remained “open for the partnership and participation of any other country” in the region.

The meeting came just hours after Washington and Tehran traded strikes for the first time in a month, breaking a lull in a war that has now run for more than six months, after the US and Israel launched attacks on Iran on February 28.

Field Marshal Asim Munir, Pakistan’s Chief of Defence Forces, and Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar had arrived in Turkiye by Sunday. Dar flew in from London, where he had just wrapped up a separate visit.

Pakistani officials had suggested in recent weeks that Egypt might also join Monday’s proceedings, not to discuss the defence pact itself, but as part of a foursome that has played a key mediating role in trying to end the US war on Iran.

The group of four last met in Amman on August 5 and, before that, in Cairo in June, where it welcomed the signing of the Pakistan-brokered Islamabad memorandum of understanding between the US and Iran.

On Monday, though, the focus was on the three countries that have inked the mutual security deal.

The Strategic Political and Defence Committee, created under the joint defence agreement Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye signed in Mecca on August 7, has now started the work of turning that political declaration — that an attack on any one of the three states will be treated as an attack on all three — into something operational.

How its institutional structure will actually function, including when the mutual-defence clause itself would be invoked, remains unclear.

Pakistan’s delegation was led by Dar, Munir and Defence Minister Khawaja Asif.

Turkiye was represented by Foreign Minister, Hakan Fidan, Defence Minister, Yasar Guler, and General Staff Chief, Selcuk Bayraktaroglu.

Saudi Arabia’s delegation included Foreign Minister, Faisal bin Farhan, Defence Minister, Khalid bin Salman and General Staff Chief, Fayyad al-Ruwaili.

According to Pakistan’s foreign ministry and Turkish officials, the agenda covered military interoperability , joint exercises, defence-industrial cooperation, including joint production and research and counterterrorism coordination.

Fidan said in an August 8 interview with the Anadolu Agency that a permanent secretariat would be based in Saudi Arabia , with its structure and remit still to be worked out among the three members.

While some have compared the mutual defence clause to NATO’s Article 5, many independent analysts have pushed back on the comparison, noting that the pact has no integrated command, standing force or joint military machinery of the kind that underpins NATO.

Tughral Yamin, a retired brigadier and senior associate at Islamabad’s Institute of Policy Studies said “an office or secretariat is a must” for the pact to become operational.

“It could be in any country, or it could be a rotating office,” he told Al Jazeera, pointing to NATO’s Supreme Headquarters Allied Powers Europe, based in Mons, Belgium.

A headquarters was already set up in Saudi Arabia, he noted, after the formation of a separate Saudi-led maritime coalition earlier this year.

Sinem Cengiz, a researcher at Qatar University’s Gulf Studies Center, told Al Jazeera that “these details need to be clear before the agreement is sent to the Turkish parliament for ratification”.

The pact’s full terms, she said, are unlikely to be made public until that process concludes.

The Istanbul meeting comes days after Munir’s fourth visit to Iran this year.

On August 24, he travelled to Tehran and met President Masoud Pezeshkian, Foreign Minister, Abbas Araghchi, and Supreme National Security Council Secretary, Mohsen Rezaei, in what Pakistan’s military described as part of its efforts to end the war.

Pakistani officials said the visit produced significant progress towards reviving the Pakistan-brokered Islamabad MoU and reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Pezeshkian, in turn, said Washington needed to change its tone.

The optimism was not fully shared in Washington. Two days later, President Donald Trump said the US was “not in a hurry” over talks with Tehran .

US Central Command struck two Revolutionary Guard rocket launchers on Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday morning, its first acknowledged strike on Iran in a month.

Iran’s Revolutionary Guard retaliated within hours, claiming that it had hit the US-operated King Hussein and Al-Azraq airbases in Jordan with ballistic missiles and the Al Menhad base in the UAE with drones, though Jordan and the UAE denied that the bases had been hit.

Yamin told Al Jazeera that Pakistan’s credibility, as both Saudi Arabia’s security partner and Tehran’s trusted interlocutor, becomes harder to sustain, “if the proposed trilateral pact evolves into an explicitly anti-Iran alliance”.

Gokhan Ereli, an international relations expert at Istanbul’s Ibn Haldun University, said the trilateral relationship predates the war, pointing to the decades-old Saudi-Pakistan security relationship and Turkiye’s own pursuit of strategic autonomy.

The real test, he said, will come once the fighting stops.

“If the joint mechanisms, institutional secretariat and industrial co-ventures outlast the current cycle of escalation, it will confirm that this pact represents a fundamental restructuring of the regional security architecture,” he told Al Jazeera.

“October 7 and the subsequent events, the fall of the Assad regime and the tensions in the Red Sea have all contributed to reshaping the region’s security landscape,” she told Al Jazeera, referring to Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza after the October 7, 2023, Hamas attacks on Israel, the ousting of Bashar al-Assad in Syria and Houthi attacks on shipping in the Red Sea.

However, she said that she did not fully agree with the characterisation of the Mecca pact as merely “symbolic” or inherently “transformative”.

Umer Karim, of the Riyadh-based King Faisal Center for Research and Islamic Studies, told Al Jazeera the war has exposed regional security vulnerabilities that go beyond Iran.

“Israel as a strategic hegemon in the region” has “implications for all three,” he told Al Jazeera, referring to Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye.

The clearest illustration came days after the Mecca signing, when Israel struck the Abu al-Duhur airbase in northern Syria, roughly 70km (43 miles) from the Turkish border, saying it was preempting a Turkish military deployment there.

Ankara condemned the strike as an attempt to undermine the trilateral pact.

Pakistan’s foreign ministry has said the pact remains open to other states.

Dar said on August 9 that the agreement was defensive in nature and did not replace any existing bilateral or multilateral arrangement.

Fidan has said that Ankara wants to eventually widen the framework beyond the three founding states.

Bangladesh has gone furthest in publicly signalling interest. State Minister for Foreign Affairs, Humayun Kabir, said in late August that Dhaka had expressed interest in the pact and that it would not be unusual for an Islamic country to join such an arrangement.

Egypt has taken part in earlier four-way security talks with Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan, but was left out of the August 7 signing.

Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan told Al Jazeera in an August 15 interview that Cairo’s accession was “possible”, saying the pact remained open to further members.

Egyptian Foreign Minister, Badr Abdelatty, has since said that Cairo is weighing constitutional and legal issues before deciding whether to join, a reference widely read as touching on Egypt’s existing treaty commitments elsewhere in the region.

Within the Gulf Cooperation Council , former Qatari Prime Minister, Sheikh Hamad bin Jassim Al-Thani, has publicly urged all GCC states to join.

Ereli named Egypt “the most strategically consequential candidate”, pointing to Cairo’s role as an anchor of Arab diplomacy and its recent rapprochement with Ankara.

Cengiz was more sceptical of Egypt’s timeline, grouping it with Syria as contingent on how the pact develops.

She pointed instead to the Gulf states as the more likely near-term movers, naming Qatar, Kuwait and Bahrain.

“They already have close relations with the signatory countries,” she said, adding that they favour diversifying their security partnerships beyond the US.

Karim, however, said any expansion would require agreement among the three founding partners on committing to a new entrant’s security, particularly if that state is itself vulnerable to regional threats.

“There can be a possibility of either Egypt, Syria or Bangladesh joining,” he said, “but it will take some time to develop the required understandings amongst all stakeholders”.

articles.title: Spectator calls low stadium flyover a top life moment: "Amazing"
articles.summary: An extremely low flyover above a rugby stadium in South Africa has left many people asking: How low is too low?
articles.body:
An extremely low flyover above a rugby stadium in South Africa has left many people asking: How low is too low?

Two passenger jets — one following the other — swept just above the packed DHL Stadium in Cape Town on Saturday, coming really close to more than 56,000 people below.

For a spectator who witnessed the passenger jets soaring overhead and captured it on video, it was a moment to remember.

"I didn't feel any danger from my side. I was just like, 'Wow, this is insane,'" said Marcel Opperman.

"It was amazing," he said. "Probably one of my top-five moments in my life."

Preliminary flight data estimates the planes cleared the stadium by only about 50 feet, which airline captain Laura Einsetler said is "really low and really tight for an airliner."

She said the full-size jets are very different from the fighter jets often seen in flyovers.

"It was just too low for this situation with this type of jet at those speeds and angles," Einsetler said.

The spectacle has roots going back more than three decades. Back in 1995, just a year after South Africa's first democratic elections, a South African Airways 747 flew low over a Johannesburg stadium during a Rugby World Cup final, as the country emerged from apartheid.

In a statement, Airlink said the planes in Saturday's flyover were operating safely, telling CBS News: "The flight demanded careful planning and rehearsal, as it required navigating at low altitude. ... The South African Civil Aviation Authority (SACAA) and Air Traffic Navigation Services provided valuable guidance, approval and support to ensure a safe flyby."

Airlink said the pilots were senior and experienced, and that they stayed within the altitude and speed limits set by the South African equivalent of the FAA.

articles.title: Afghan general who led last-ditch effort to stop Taliban takeover now drives Uber in Washington
articles.summary: US News: Afghan General Haibatullah Alizai, who led a last-ditch effort to resist the Taliban takeover in 2021, now drives an Uber in Washington DC after being.
articles.body: Afghan General Haibatullah Alizai, who led a last-ditch effort to resist the Taliban takeover in 2021, now drives an Uber in Washington DC after being granted asylum in the US.In an interview with CBS’ Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan, Alizai spoke about his final days in Afghanistan, his evacuation by US forces and his life as an immigrant in the US.Alizai, the last chief of staff of the Afghan army, fled Afghanistan in August 2021 as the US military was completing its withdrawal. He had been trying to form a resistance against the Taliban when US personnel told him that the base was being closed and everyone had to leave within minutes.He boarded a US military C-17 in civilian clothes without initially knowing where he was being taken. The aircraft eventually landed in Kuwait.Alizai later received asylum in the US, where he described his new life as that of an immigrant. Finding employment proved difficult because of extensive background checks and other processes, he said. He now drives for Uber in Washington DC.The former general also remains separated from his wife and three sons, who have asylum in India. He said he cannot travel outside the US and does not know when he will be able to see his family again.Reflecting on his relationship with the US, Alizai said Afghan and American soldiers had “shared blood” over two decades of war. Despite the Taliban takeover and the collapse of the Afghan government, he said he still had hope.“We have shared blood together for 20 years,” Alizai said. “Whatever happened, still, this is the right side. I have some hope.”Alizai had spent his final days in Afghanistan working with US forces at Kabul airport during the chaotic evacuation. He said Afghan intelligence had warned of a possible Islamic State Khorasan (ISKP) attack around August 22 or 23, before the August 26 suicide bombing that killed 170 Afghans and 13 US service members.Looking back, Alizai said he considered the 20-year US-Afghan military partnership worthwhile, arguing that preventing terrorist attacks on US soil was among its key objectives.The US withdrawal from Afghanistan was completed on August 30, 2021, ending America's longest war and leaving the country under Taliban control.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: SEC lawyers, Lane Kiffin and Death Valley: College football’s Week 1 is set for for fireworks
articles.summary: Clemson-LSU in Death Valley, Notre Dame vs. Wisconsin at Lambeau Field and more highlight five days of college football over Labor Day weekend.
articles.body: The appetizer that was week zero in college football certainly delivered in a time of desperation for fans across the country wanting just a taste of what is to come this season. But after seven long months of waiting, the main course finally arrives this week, headlined by Clemson’s trip to Baton Rouge for a Saturday night showdown in Death Valley — and Lane Kiffin’s LSU debut. COLLEGE ATHLETICS' LATEST MESS: COURT ORDERS SAY PRO ATHLETES CAN PLAY, BUT SEC AND BIG TEN READY TO FIGHT Trust me, I understand fans are sick of hearing about the ongoing court battles between athletes from the 2022 class and the SEC. But there is another fight brewing in Baton Rouge on Thursday morning that will draw plenty of attention. SEC bringing their lawyers to Baton Rouge for a courtroom battle on Thursday When plaintiffs in the Louisiana case added the SEC to their amended complaint over the weekend, taking aim at Conference commissioner Greg Sankey for his part in enacting new guidelines approved by member schools, it was only a matter of time before this route was taken by attorneys. Now, before LSU takes on Clemson on Saturday, a courtroom will be the setting for the latest round between class of 2022 athletes and the NCAA. NCAA WINS TENTH CIRCUIT 'STAY', BUT FACES MORE ELIGIBILITY LAWSUITS FROM 2022 CLASS ATHLETES IN CHAOTIC TIME On Sunday night, OutKick asked the SEC about being added to the case, which the conference then provided a statement noting they would be inside the Baton Rouge courthouse in order to argue their case. "The order entered against the SEC and Commissioner Sankey is a temporary restraining order, not a final ruling on the merits, the conference noted. "The SEC and Commissioner Sankey are prepared to contest the allegations in the plaintiffs’ petition at Thursday morning’s hearing and defend the SEC’s rights as a voluntary association to fulfill its mission to its member institutions. In the meantime, the SEC and Commissioner Sankey will continue to comply with the Court’s order. Following the hearing, the SEC will carefully review the Court’s decision and determine the appropriate next steps" What does that final sentence mean? GOVERNOR LANDRY BACKS LANE KIFFIN, LSU IN FIGHT WITH SEC: ‘DON’T HATE THE PLAYER, HATE THE GAME’ Well, if an injunction is granted for the athletes in this case and some of those athletes take the field on Saturday night for LSU against Clemson, or listed on Friday's final roster report, the SEC would then have to make a decision on how to enforce their own rules pertaining to athletes with NFL ties. OutKick will have you covered this week from both the courthouse on Thursday morning, and inside Tiger Stadium on Saturday night. We have officially made it to Week 1 of the college football season Thankfully, we had a number of games this past weekend that delivered enough drama to get us through the next four days. I don't think many of us, myself included, expected Bill Belichick to lead his North Carolina team to a win over TCU in Ireland. But, I'd also say that it's hard to take away a lot from that one game, besides the fact that Sonny Dykes is desperately missing quarterback Josh Hoover after he transferred to Indiana. BILL BELICHICK FINALLY PROVIDES UNC WITH A PULSE, BUT NOW HE HAS TO EARN THAT $10 MILLION PAYCHECK But, the Tar Heels certainly needed a win to create a spark in Chapel Hill before having to play Notre Dame and Clemson over the next month. Heck, they really just needed a win, which obviously was accomplished. Also, how about Memphis going to Las Vegas and upsetting UNLV? Monster win for Charles Huff, which left Dan Mullen complaining about his own fans starting the 'wave' while his offense was on the field. Yes, this actually transpired, Mullen was upset. FROM FSU TO DAN MULLEN, HERE ARE THREE 'OVERREACTIONS' FROM WEEK ZERO OF THE COLLEGE FOOTBALL SEASON Now, looking ahead to a jam-packed schedule this week, it all starts in Atlanta on Thursday night, as Deion Sanders will roam the Georgia Tech sidelines in primetime. Here's a look at which games I've got my eye on this week. We have spent seven months talking about Lane Kiffin leading LSU out of the tunnel at Tiger Stadium, and it finally comes to fruition Saturday night in Death Valley. Expectations are sky-high across Louisiana, and nationally, for this LSU team. But this is also a measuring-stick game for Dabo Swinney and Clemson. Can he lead the Tigers into one of the sport’s most hostile environments and leave with a victory? Predictions are coming later this week, but that is a tall task for Clemson. ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW! Here we go. The Fighting Irish will face the Badgers at Lambeau Field to begin what should be a season that ends in the College Football Playoff for Notre Dame. We will also get a fresh look at Heisman Trophy candidate CJ Carr, while Luke Fickell and Wisconsin could have their hands full trying to keep this Fighting Irish offense out of the end zone. A potentially massive season awaits Marcus Freeman and his team. NCAA CREATED THIS MESS, NOW LSU SET TO MAKE DAE’QUAN WRIGHT COLLEGE FOOTBALL’S FIRST NFL RETURNEE Year One for Pete Golding as Ole Miss’ full-time head coach begins with a neutral-site matchup against Louisville in Nashville. We know what the Rebels have on offense, with Trinidad Chambliss at quarterback and Kewan Lacy back for what could be another highlight-filled season at running back. But don’t sleep on Louisville in this one. I’m just saying. After a lackluster showing against New Mexico State this past weekend, Florida State better figure out how to contain SMU quarterback Kevin Jennings. If it doesn’t, this could be the beginning of a stretch that puts Mike Norvell’s job in serious jeopardy over the next two months. Go ahead and get all of those chores done now, or figure out how to get out of an event planned by your family or significant other. College football is officially back, and I can promise there will be an upset this weekend that Vegas isn’t predicting. articles.title: 1,800 People Help Pull a 400-Ton Japanese Castle Back to Its Original Site
articles.summary: Can you imagine trying to move a 400-ton castle tower by pulling on a rope? About 1,800 people in Japan recently did just that and moved the building more th...
articles.body:
Can you imagine trying to move a 400-ton castle tower by pulling on a rope? About 1,800 people in Japan recently did just that and moved the building more than seven feet over two days.

The unusual castle pull took place Aug. 22 and 23 at Hirosaki Castle in Aomori Prefecture. It was part of a decade-long project to repair the stone wall beneath the castle's keep.

Smithsonian Magazine reported that the castle's main tower, called a keep, moved about four feet on Saturday and another 3.5 feet on Sunday. The three-story wooden building stayed intact throughout the move.

More than 8,000 people applied for the 1,800 available spots. The selected participants came from across Japan and from as far away as Southeast Asia, Europe and North America.

Embedded media follows. Please allow a moment for it to load.

To pull off this impressive move, groups of about 80 people took turns using nearly 100-foot ropes while the building sat on rails and rollers. The method is called hikiya, and it allows a building to be moved without taking it apart.

The Guardian reported that the keep's 2015 move was the first citizen-led hikiya and the first time the method had been used to move a castle in a century.

The hand-pulling is scheduled to continue through the end of August. Around 4,100 people will help move the keep a total of 16 feet before machinery handles the remaining 240 feet by the end of 2026.

The keep was moved approximately 256 feet away from its base in 2015. This allowed crews to repair a stone wall that had been damaged during an earthquake in 1983.

The wall was finished in December 2024, with all 2,185 stones returned to their original positions. Archaeological work also uncovered parts of older walls, a well, and drainage structures beneath the castle grounds.

Visitors Will Have to Wait To Go Inside Until 2033

Hirosaki Castle was completed in 1611, but its original five-story keep burned down after lightning struck it in 1627. Construction on the current three-story keep began in 1810. Today, it is one of only 12 surviving feudal-era castle towers in Japan. In fact, it is the only one remaining in the country's northeastern Tōhoku region.

Even after the keep returns to its original base later this year, visitors will not be able to go inside. It will be covered while additional preservation work is completed and is expected to reopen in 2033.
